In a superconformal theory, operators are organized into representations labeled by
quantum numbers such as spin J, R-charge R, and scaling dimension A.
Normally, A can receive quantum corrections:
A = Aclassical + v(9),
where y(g) changes continuously with the coupling g.
For a BPS operator, supersymmetry forces an exact relation
A = f(R,J)
Since R and J are discrete and fixed for that representation, A is fixed too. So
ordinary perturbative quantum corrections cannot move it continuously.
Could A jump to another allowed value? Yes, but then the operator would have to join
or leave a different representation, typically through multiplet recombination at a
special point. That is not the usual small quantum correction to the same BPS
operator; it means the representation structure has changed, and sometimes this can
correspond to moving to a different phase/branch or effectively a different theory.

String-gas cosmology asks whether a hot early universe filled with string states could
use this physics to determine which dimensions become large.
One famous idea is that winding strings have to encounter and annihilate one another
before a dimension can expand freely.
Two string worldsheets generically intersect efficiently only if there are sufficiently
few large spatial dimensions.
This led Brandenberger and Vafa to propose a mechanism suggesting why perhaps
only three spatial dimensions became macroscopic.
It is an interesting string-cosmology scenario, not an experimentally established
explanation of why we observe three large dimensions.
